resources.string: Encrypts the API traffic with the phone\'s own certificate. Plain http:// clients stop working: give them the fingerprint below.
Certificate unavailable: %1$s. The API stays off rather than run without encryption.

The certificate comes from the phone, not from a public authority. A client either trusts it once (Export, then curl --cacert or Python verify=) or pins the public key. Both stay valid when the phone changes address. Check that the fingerprint matches before trusting a file.
The fingerprint and the pin change. Scripts and AI agents that trust or pin the current certificate are refused until you give them the new one.
The token is read from the BIMMERDATA_TOKEN environment variable.
HTTPS with a self-signed certificate: pin the public key %1$s (curl --pinnedpubkey) or trust the certificate whose SHA-256 is %2$s.
